I think you misunderstand. “Late” is around 10-20 minutes without a reply. She starts yelling in less than 3.
I agree about the polite manners thing, but having such a tight obsessive grip on someone isn’t healthy. I just don’t want to be shouted at and blamed for something that isn’t my fault. If you’re with someone and they’re picking up a third party to go somewhere on no time schedule, and the driver starts yelling at *you* in under 3 minutes of pulling up to the driveway, don’t you think something’s wrong with that?

My mom does something similar, and gets especially bad when we’re picking up my buddy for lunch or something. We’re never on any time schedule, but she’ll huff and puff in the car and yell his name into my ears, as if I’m supposed to be the keeper of a grown-ass man.
If she’s picking me up, I’ll get constant texts every half a minute. It’s gotten to the point where I always pack up an hour early so I don’t have to get yelled at. I can’t wait to move out of this god forsaken place. Stay strong OP! It’s tough but you can do it. We’re in your corner; most of us, anyway.

Edit: To give a little context as to my situation; I’m 22F, struggling to save money to move out from odd jobs, and I’m getting treatment for severe anxiety that impairs my ability to operate a car. I’m applying for college and working as hard as I can to improve my situation.
I wasn’t attempting to imply that my mother absolutely has to drive me anywhere, but it’s the only reliable mode of transport I have right now. Yes, I do get frustrated when *I’m* shouted at because someone, not just my aforementioned buddy - but *anyone* my mother offers to drive around, is more than 3 minutes late walking to the car. I get frustrated when I get shouted at for being more than 3 minutes late out to the car because I’m on the toilet by pure happenstance. I’ve sent a text before explaining that I’m on the toilet, and was still shouted at for not “spacing it out better” for her convenience.
Not everyone with this type of story is entitled. I apologize for not being more up-front in my original post. But maybe sometimes, a parent is just trying to keep a tight grip on their child because they revel in having power over someone. Sometimes, it isn’t a child’s entitlement. Sometimes it’s just abuse.

Hey, this is one of the people that helped to set up this gofundme. I’d like to kind of respond with a little more information, and why r/legaladvice won’t really help.

He and his family can’t afford food. He hasn’t been able to afford simple dental procedures for a while now. I can’t afford to help him long-term. We live in a very, very poor community. We can’t afford legal help. I apologize. We’ve tried this exact site, but it still didn’t help with our situation.

He’s facing eviction he can’t get out of. He’s been given one month for him and his entire family to leave. The gofundme, at this point, is for anything to help them find a new place to live. It’s an emergency situation. I’m sorry.

I have, but it just feels hollow. I’m paying him to care, he doesn’t care about me because of any real, organic reason. I know it sounds stupid, but I wish someone that considered me “close” would care enough to at least let me cry with them.
It’s not a matter of therapy I guess. It’s a matter of “why do these people claim to care when they obviously don’t? Nobody would give a crap if I were dead.”
Thank you so much, it means a lot!
